chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Do not regard an expression uttered by any person as evil if you can find it capable of bearing some good.
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim interpret the words of others to avoid negative assumptions?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *husn al-zann* (good opinion), urging believers to default to benevolence when interpreting others' utterances. This teaching serves as a spiritual safeguard against suspicion (*khabath al-zann*) and fosters social harmony by prioritizing plausible positive meanings over hasty negative judgments. It reflects the Shia emphasis on purifying the heart from the disease of cynicism, which is often cited as a barrier to divine proximity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 360. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Do not regard an expression uttered by any person as evil if you can find it capable of bearing some good.
